title: Book Two · Chapter 123: The Quiet Answer
story:
Ronan reaches the reading room early on Tuesday. He has a question about his own practice. It is about one short word. He has written his question down.

Two other pupils are already waiting. Miss Wu has work from three groups on her table. She points to the chairs.

“I can give each of you a few minutes.”

Ronan sits at the end. He reads his question again. In the story, a boy carries a chair from one room to another. The last line says he brings it back before dinner. Ronan knows which chair the boy carries. But he is not sure where the chair is at the end.

When his turn comes, he opens the story.

“I know he moves it,” he says. “I do not know where it is at the end.”

Miss Wu gives him two little blocks.

“This is the first room. This is the second. Use your finger for the chair.”

He moves his finger from one block to the other.

“Now read the last line.”

He reads it and moves back to the first block.

“Here?”

“Which words tell you?”

“Brings it back.”

She asks him to read the next short story. In that one, a girl lends a cup to a neighbour. The neighbour brings it back in the evening.

Ronan puts his finger beside the girl's house.

“The cup comes here again.”

“Yes.”

The few minutes are over. Miss Wu puts away the blocks. Ronan looks at his question paper.

“Is that too easy a question?” he asks.

“Did you know the answer?”

“Not clearly.”

“Then you had a reason to ask.”

The next pupil takes his place. Ronan goes to a side table and tries a third page by himself. This time he draws a small arrow, then says the final place in a whole sentence.

Mei sits at the next table. She has two long paragraphs about a picture collection. She is choosing one clear fact for a label.

“Are you drawing?” Ronan asks.

“Reading first. I need the right place name.”

He looks at her page. It is harder than his. For a moment he wants to hide his own arrows.

Mei points to one of them.

“What does that mean?”

“He returns the chair to the first room.”

“Clear.”

She turns back to her work. Ronan leaves his page flat on the table.

At home that evening, Dad asks him to bring a small bowl back from the kitchen. Ronan fetches it, then laughs.

“What?” Dad asks.

“Nothing. I know where you want it.”

He puts the bowl beside Dad's cup. Mum takes a piece of bread from it and asks for another.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

back＝回来；lend＝借给；neighbour＝邻居；clearly＝清楚地。

## 理解问题

1. 老师用什么帮Ronan理解back？
2. Mei在为标签做什么准备？

## 读句子

**He / puts the bowl / beside Dad's cup.** 他／把碗／放在Dad杯子旁边。
